content:
Earlier in June this year, we reported on three cases involving apps from a US-sanctioned Russian bank appearing on the App Store in a different guise. Two months later, another similar example has topped the iPhone App Store chart.

K8CHEN PRO is the latest case. On its App Store listing page, it masquerades as a kitchen design tool with augmented reality (AR) functionality.

But the moment you open the app, the flaws are immediately exposed. The privacy policy link on the App Store page reveals that its content was auto-generated by "Free Privacy Policy Generator" — which on its own is already a major red flag.

Regardless, this app is undoubtedly the client app of T-Bank. What baffles me is how such apps can repeatedly pass App Store review.

When these apps rocket up the App Store rankings precisely because they have become widely known, anyone with eyes can see they should never have been listed in the first place. It is truly bewildering.

For the other cases reported in June, you can read about them here and here.

Update: Sure enough, the app has now been pulled from the App Store.
